scores.evidence_span: Identify 1–2 professors at your university in Jiangsu who work on AI, ideally with interdisciplinary applications.
scores.rationale: The preference for applications is partly expressed in supervisor identification, but applied, implementation-heavy, or system-building research is not explicitly established as a program-selection priority.

No source or evidence class is selected specifically to evaluate whether programs support applied or system-building research. Paper reading and replication are preparation activities, not a preference-specific program-evaluation route.

scores.evidence_span: **Research Strengths:** Applied AI, Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing, and Smart City technologies.
scores.rationale: The Asia section identifies relevant research areas, but supplies no concrete program feature, project, facility, or other verifiable fact showing how a named option supports implementation-heavy research.
Descriptions of European theoretical depth and Max Planck foundational research do not establish that any option conducts purely abstract, theory-only research.
The report does not directly compare applied research with theory-only research on a common decision axis or identify a consequential difference between them.

Named destinations are recommended for funding, lifestyle, and safety, while research directions are recommended for interdisciplinary fit and perceived competition. No named option is selected explicitly because it supports applied or system-building research.
No otherwise viable named option is downgraded because it favors theory-only research. The criticism of pure deep learning concerns saturation, not theoretical orientation.

scores.evidence_span: Read 2–3 papers per week during your morning routine. Replicate their code in PyCharm/VS Code during the evenings.
scores.rationale: Replicating the code of selected research papers is a concrete, executable implementation activity in the preparation plan.

scores.evidence_span: Use your productive evening blocks (when you use VS Code/PyCharm) strictly for lab experiments, coding, and paper drafting.
scores.rationale: The report explicitly allocates evening work blocks to activities that include implementation and experiments, providing a usable scheduling rule rather than merely recommending applied work.
No concrete condition is given under which theory-only research would become the better choice.
The report contains implementation activities but no visible chain connecting an applied-research preference to supporting evidence and then to a resulting decision or action.
